what point is it generally good at to take a video game project and first show an alpha look? what level of completion is generally considered to be "complete enough"?

Do you mean playable or unplayable? In the former it needs to, you know, be playable. You need to have a segment that can be played through without issues. In the latter, well, make it look like it's the former.

I'd first show an alpha when there's something to show. Sounds stupid, but there needs to be some solid substance on offer. It doesn't have to look amazing, but something that gets the message across fairly swiftly. Concepts only go so far.

I'd say a 'complete game' is when it's fully functioning, with all the main elements/mechanics are in place. That's when you bugfix (the remianing ones anyway), and polish the game to look presentable.

When it's playable without too many crashes and bugs

Depends on the genre, to be honest. Making demos of gameplay-weak games is generally useless. On the other hand it can be really interesting to show the concepts and mechanics at work in games with actual mechanics, especially if some your mechanics are new to your audience (and they should be). An alpha isn't a dev blog. It has to show to the potential customer that you actually have a clue what you're doing, especially when it comes to game design. And that means other aspects don't have to be very polished. You do have to consider that people will criticize placeholders regardless, especially if you present it like everything is a placeholder. Insist on the stuff you have closest to what you think is production-ready state. If you don't offer your audience something to focus on, they'll get bored and nitpick. It's sadly frequent to present a demo when it's just a collection of placeholders haphazardly cobbled together to meet a deadline. You need to have something inside the demo that could be the focal point of a speech you make about it, otherwise there's no point. In fact, you should practice making a speech about your demo showcasing what you want to talk about. If there's nothing to talk about in particular, your demo is not good enough.
